text.en: A rhombus has four equal sides. The book gives a rhombus cut into triangular pieces. What shapes can you make from them?

A rhombus is a shape with all four sides equal. Cut it into triangles and join two triangles to make new shapes.
A triangle with 2 equal sides is called an isosceles triangle. Fold it in half and you will see that it has 2 equal angles.
A triangle with all 3 sides equal is an equilateral triangle, and its 3 angles are equal too.
A triangle with no equal sides is a scalene triangle. Check whether any of its angles are equal.
Using the pieces we can also make kites and parallelograms, and with 3 triangles a 3-sided, 4-sided or 5-sided shape.
The tangram set at the end of the book has 7 pieces. Cut them out, name them and use them to make figures.
A circle drawn with a compass has a centre, and every point on it is the same distance from the centre.
